newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV 96 prelim pre-tax hits record high.
newsitem.headline: OMV 96 prelim pre-tax hits record high.

text.p: Austria's biggest industrial concern OMV AG said on Wednesday its preliminary pre-tax earnings soared 39 percent to a new record in 1996 as all divisions put in a solid performance.

The oil and chemicals group reported a pre-tax profit of 2.9 billion schillings ($251 million), up from the record 2.09 billion schillings it posted in 1995. Earnings before interest and tax climbed to 2.9 billion schillings from 2.19 billion.
A government freeze of tax credits on past losses had dampened net profit growth, however, OMV said in a statement.
The firm reported a preliminary 1.9 billion schillings net profit, up from 1.73 billion, and said it planned to raise its dividend payment by three schillings to 23.
"All six business divisions contributed to this positive result," OMV said.
The results were at the upper end of analysts' forecasts.

OMV said exploration and production benefited from high crude oil prices while its gas division remained the earnings powerhouse. Refining, marketing, chemicals and plastics also ended the year in the black, OMV continued.
OMV shares were 5.5 schillings up at 1,335 in pre-market trade. ($ = 11.56 Austrian Schillings)
